newsitem.title: UK: British government urged to replace royal yacht.
newsitem.headline: British government urged to replace royal yacht.

text.p: The British government was on Thursday urged to approve replacement of the royal yacht Britannia, due to be decommissioned after 44 years afloat, because of the ship's success in promoting Britain abroad.

A group of rival British marine designers and their backers came together at the London International Boat Show to make the joint appeal for a successor to Queen Elizabeth's yacht, which they said would raise Britain's profile abroad, creating jobs and income through trade deals.
The near 6,000-tonne Britannia's days are numbered due to its running costs and the government has not yet decided on whether to replace it.
Those lobbying for a new ship said it had been invaluable in promoting British trade, contributing two billion pounds ($3.4 billion) to Britain's earnings over the last 10 years.
Andrew Buxton, chairman of British banking giant Barclays, was among those supporting the proposals, adding that he had led several trade missions aboard the Britannia.
"It is able to attract a very high quality trade audience. When the royal yacht sits in a harbour, people want to come aboard," he told Reuters.

Estimates of what a new yacht might cost varied from 70 to 100 million pounds, but Buxton said this would be easy to finance under the government's Private Finance Initiative (PFI) scheme, which brings private investment into public projects.

All proponents of replacements for Britannia, ranging from a royal sail training ship to a combined royal yacht and cruise ship, stressed the new vessel would be built in Britain and would demonstrate British state-of-the-art marine expertise. ($1=.5870 Pound)
